subject: Temporary throughput elevation with tiered rolloff
messages:
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: alex@brightlane.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-21T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Request: short-term throughput bump for Brightlane launch

Alex —

Congrats on the launch date next week. We ran your staging traffic against production and see a concentrated burst window that will exceed the current quota by ~3x for a 6‑hour window on launch day. To avoid throttles we can provision a temporary throughput elevation.

Proposal (high level):
- 6 hours of elevated qps (sustained window) on 2026-10-28 UTC window
- Blended per-token rate for elevated window (15% premium)
- Automatic tiered rollback: 50% uplift day+1, 25% day+2, then back to committed level

I attached a quick usage summary and a PO draft so procurement can see costs. If this looks reasonable I can loop in finance and legal to finalize the PO and waiver language.

Next step: Can Paula confirm whether a one-off PO with a short addendum works for Brightlane, or do we need a standing amendment?

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: oct-launch-usage-summary.csv (CSV summary), Brightlane_PO_draft.pdf (PO + proposed billing terms)
From: alex@brightlane.com (Alex Chen)
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: paula@brightlane.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term throughput bump for Brightlane launch

Ben —

Appreciate the heads up and the analysis. A few clarifying Qs from engineering and procurement:

1) Is the 15% premium applied only to tokens consumed during the elevated window, or to the whole day's usage? We prefer per-token window billing.
2) We need a firm upper cap (hard ceiling) for that 6‑hour lift — can you state the exact qps numbers and the safety stop if we hit 150% of the predicted peak?
3) Procurement: a single one-off PO is fine, but we need net 45 payment terms and a statement of work-level description for auditing. Paula — can you confirm the contact for PO receipt?

Also, please confirm whether any additional latency SLO or routing costs apply for the elevated capacity.

On timing, we need to have the PO in-hand by Friday EOD to get finance approvals.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Head of Engineering, Brightlane Labs
alex@brightlane.com

---- Original message quoted below ----
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: alex@brightlane.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-22T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term throughput bump for Brightlane launch

Alex / Paula —

Thanks for the questions. Quick answers inline: 

> 1) Is the 15% premium applied only to tokens consumed during the elevated window, or to the whole day's usage?

The uplift rate applies only to tokens consumed during the elevated window (the billing is metered by token/time window). We will tag requests by window to make the audit clean.

> 2) We need a firm upper cap (hard ceiling) for that 6‑hour lift — can you state the exact qps numbers and the safety stop if we hit 150% of the predicted peak?

We can set a hard ceiling at 1.8x of the predicted peak (safe step). If Brightlane hits 150% of predicted peak we will automatically throttle to protect stability and notify your SREs; we can also act on a manual escalation to push beyond that if authorized in writing. We'll include the exact qps number in the addendum once you confirm predicted peak number (please confirm the peak qps figure from your load test).

> 3) Procurement: a single one-off PO is fine, but we need net 45 payment terms and a statement of work-level description for auditing. Paula — can you confirm the contact for PO receipt?

Net 45 is acceptable for a one-off addendum — we'll pass to Finance and Legal for standard approval. PO receipt address: invoices@redwood.com.

Latency SLO: no additional latency surcharge; the elevated capacity will be served from the same dedicated pool with the same SLOs.

Ben — can you produce an amended PO with net 45 and a short SOW paragraph and return to Paula by Thursday so they have time to route internally?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachments: none
From: paula@brightlane.com (Paula Moreno)
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, alex@brightlane.com
Date: 2026-10-26T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term throughput bump for Brightlane launch — PO and signature

Kimberly / Ben —

Thanks for the updates and the revised PO. We reviewed with Finance — Brightlane is comfortable with the per-window billing and the 15% uplift applied only to that window. A couple of final asks: 

- Please add the hard ceiling qps number: 12,000 rps for the elevated window (this aligns with our load test). If the ceiling is reached we accept automatic throttling with a notification-to-escalation path.
- Include a single‑sentence SOW line: "Temporary elevated throughput for launch day 2026-10-28 with tiered rollback over 48 hours."
- Payment terms: Net 45 to invoices@brightlane.com (we will route once DocuSign arrives).

Attached is the signed PO template (signed by Procurement) — we need Redwood's countersignature via DocuSign.

Alex — please confirm you have internal agreement on the 12,000 rps ceiling and that SRE is ready for the escalation workflow.

Thanks — Paula
Paula Moreno
Procurement Lead, Brightlane Labs
paula@brightlane.com
